title: Durable Assimilation Record Retrieval Foundation
objective: Establish the authoritative durable retrieval boundary for generated Assimilation record sets persisted by ASSIMILATION-001 so complete records can be reopened after process termination while preserving exact identities, provenance, deterministic semantics, filesystem containment, raw-source immutability, and subsystem authority boundaries.
architecturalContext: ASSIMILATION-001 durably persists complete generated record sets under the dedicated generated-records filesystem boundary.
The existing persistence interface is write-only and currently exposes no authoritative retrieval operation.

Existing Assimilation validators cover source assets, extraction, segments, classifications, identifier formats, and derived-object derivation semantics, but there is no standalone TransformationRecord validator.
Retrieval must treat persisted JSON as untrusted durable data and fail closed rather than returning unchecked type casts.
Knowledge execution and orchestration remain separate downstream concerns and are excluded from this objective.
acceptanceCriteria: The existing generated-record persistence boundary exposes an additive typed retrieval operation by authoritative asset identifier.
Retrieval resolves the same traversal-safe generated-record path convention established by ASSIMILATION-001.

A successful retrieval returns the complete persisted asset, extraction, segment, classification, transformation, and derived-object record set while preserving exact identifiers and serialized values.
Persisted JSON is parsed as untrusted data and validated before being returned as an AssimilationGeneratedRecordSet.
Existing reusable Assimilation validators and identifier predicates are composed where applicable rather than duplicating subsystem validation logic.
TransformationRecord structure and cross-record relationships are validated narrowly inside the persistence boundary without modifying deterministic pipeline or derivation behavior.
Retrieval fails closed for missing files, malformed JSON, structurally invalid records, invalid identifiers, schema/version violations, or inconsistent cross-record identities/provenance.
Retrieved asset identity must match the asset identifier requested by the caller.
Transformation and derived-object linkage must remain internally consistent, including transformation output identity and derived-object transformation reference.
Traversal-shaped asset identifiers remain contained within generated-record storage and cannot escape the configured persistence root.
Retrieval is read-only and does not modify persisted generated records, immutable raw-source storage, or source-asset provenance.
Existing persistence overwrite protection and ASSIMILATION-001 behavior remain unchanged.

Knowledge execution, Knowledge persistence, production Knowledge handoff, orchestration changes, databases, remote storage, network access, model invocation, credential access, commit, push, and deployment are not introduced.
requiredTests: ASSIMILATION-002 missing, malformed, invalid, inconsistent, and traversal-safe retrieval tests
approvalBoundaries: Do not modify raw-source ingestion or immutable source storage.
Do not modify production Assimilation, pipeline, extraction, segmentation, classification, derivation, Knowledge, or orchestration boundaries.
Do not introduce database, remote storage, network, model, credential, execution-authorization, commit, or publication authority.
Do not weaken validation or return unchecked parsed JSON as trusted Assimilation records.
commitMessage: ASSIMILATION-002: Build durable assimilation record retrieval foundation
